The second: to magnify its status and exalt its rank, by beginning with its attribution to Him.

The first: that is, their alternation in length and shortness.

(p-261) The second: the alternation of them by the going of one and the coming of the other.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 45, verse 6–11:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar⁠﴾ has three interpretations:

One of them: al-Affak (the liar), i.e., the one who lies much. This is said by Ibn Jurayj.

The second: that he is the one who denies his Lord.

The third: that he is the soothsayer (kahin), said by Qatadah.

﴿Who hears the signs of Allah recited to him⁠﴾ meaning the Qur'an.

﴿Then persists in arrogance⁠﴾ has two interpretations:

One of them: he maintains his polytheism, arrogant toward obedience to his Lord, and this is the meaning of the saying of Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: that al-Islrar (persistence) upon a thing is the firm resolve upon it, and it is derived from "sarra al-surrah" (he tied the purse) when he tied it shut. This is said by Ibn Isa.

(p-262) ﴿As if he had not heard it⁠﴾ in not being admonished by it and not accepting it.

﴿So give him tidings of a painful punishment⁠﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: this verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 45, verses 12–15:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: they do not attain the blessings of Allah. This is the view of Mujahid.

Second: they do not fear the punishment of Allah. This is the view of al-Kalbi and Muqatil.

Third: they do not hope for the victory of Allah, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. This is the view of Ibn Bahr.

Regarding the meaning of "the Days of Allah" there are two interpretations:

One of them: they are the days of His bounty and His retribution in this world, because there are no such days in the Hereafter, and "days" here denotes a period of time, although they are days in the literal sense.

In the sentence there is an omitted command, and its implied meaning is: Say to those who believe, "Forgive," so that they (the believers) will forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah.

Forgiveness (al-ghufran) here means pardon and leaving off retaliation for harm.

Al-Kalbi related that this verse was revealed concerning Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when a man among the polytheists insulted him, and he intended to seize the man, but when this verse was revealed concerning him, he refrained from him.

Regarding the abrogation (naskh) of this verse there are two views: (p-263)

One of them: that it remains in force concerning pardoning harm in matters other than religion.

The second: that it has been abrogated. Regarding what abrogated it there are two views:

One of them: His saying, Glorified is He, ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. This is the view of Qatadah.

The second: His saying ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against, because they have been wronged﴾. This is the view of Abu Salih.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 45, verses 16–20:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter﴾. Regarding this there are two views:

One: the mention of the Messenger and the signs of his prophethood.

The second: the explanation of the lawful and the unlawful. This was said by al-Suddi.

﴿And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them﴾. Regarding this there are two views:

One: after Yusha' ibn Nun, so some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. This is related by al-Naqqash.

The second: after God had informed them of what is in the Torah.

﴿Out of mutual insolence﴾ (baghyan baynahum). Regarding this there are three views:

One: out of seeking leadership and arrogance, refusing to submit to the truth. This is related by Ibn Isa.

The second: out of rebellion against the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by denying what their own Book contains of his prophethood and his description. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The third (p-264): that they desired the world and its ease, so they altered their Book, making lawful whatever they wished and unlawful whatever they wished. This was said by Yahya ibn Adam.

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Then We placed you on a path of the matter﴾. That is, on a way of the religion, like the path (shari'ah) that leads to water. From this comes the word shari' (legislator/one who prescribes), because it is a path to the goal.

Regarding the meaning of shari'ah there are four sayings:

One: that it is the religion. This was said by Ibn Zayd, because it is the path to salvation.

The second: that it is the obligations, the prescribed limits, the commands and the prohibitions. This was said by Qatadah, because they are the path to the religion.

The third: that it is the clear evidence. This was said by Muqatil, because it is the path of truth.

The fourth: the Sunnah. This is related by al-Kalbi, because he follows the way of the prophets before him.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds?﴾ That is, they have acquired polytheism (shirk).

Al-Kalbi said: Those meant by this verse are Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, and al-Walid ibn Utbah.

﴿That We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: Al-Kalbi said they are meant as Ali ibn Abi Talib, Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and Ubaydah ibn al-Harith, when they came out against them on the day of Badr and killed them.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Have you seen one who takes his own desire as his god?﴾ There are three opinions regarding it:

The first: "Have you seen one who takes as his religion whatever his desire inclines to, so that he does not desire anything without mounting it?" This was said by Ibn Abbas.

(p-265) The second: "Have you seen one who makes his god, whom he worships, whatever his desire and his preference incline to? So when he finds something good and is inclined to it, he takes it as a god." This was said by Ikrimah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: One of them would worship a stone, and when he saw something better than it, he would discard it and worship the other.

The third: "Have you seen one who submits to his desire as he submits to his god and object of worship?" This is a wonder for people of intellect at this ignorance.

﴿And Allah has led him astray knowingly﴾: Regarding it there are two interpretations:

One: He found him astray. This was related by Ibn Bahr.

The second: Its meaning is that he went astray from Allah.

From this is the verse of the poet:

"Grant me, a man from among you, who has lost his camel, that he has a protection, for protection is abundant."

That is, his camel strayed from him.

Regarding His words ﴿knowingly﴾ there are two aspects:

One: knowingly, that he is astray. This was said by Muqatil.

The second: this was said by Ibn Abbas, meaning in His foreknowledge, that he would go astray.

﴿And has sealed over his hearing and his heart﴾: That is, He sealed his hearing so that he does not hear admonition, and sealed his heart so that he does not comprehend guidance.

﴿And placed over his sight a covering﴾, so that he does not see right guidance.

Then, in this statement there are two aspects:

One: that it comes in the form of a report about their conditions.

The second: that it comes in the form of a supplication against them with that.

Ibn Juraij related that it was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Qays of the Ghayatilah, and al-Dahhak related that it was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 45, verses 24–26:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And they say: "There is nothing but our life of this world"﴾. This saying of theirs is a denial of the Hereafter, a rejection of resurrection, and a negation of recompense.

﴿We die and we live﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

The first: it is inverted (muqaddam wa mu'akhkhar, a transposition of words in the sentence), and its intended sense is "we live and we die." This is also how it is read in the recitation (qira'ah) of Ibn Mas'ud.

The second: it is in its natural order, and in its interpretation there are two views:

The first: "We die, and our children live," as said by al-Kalbi.

The second: "Some of us die."

﴿And nothing destroys us but time (al-dahr)﴾. Concerning this there are four interpretations:

The first: "And nothing destroys us but the lifespan (al-'umr)," as said by Qatadah. He recited the verse of the poet:

*For every matter that comes upon a day, there is a cause, and time, in it and in its turning, is a wonder.*

The second: "And nothing destroys us but the age (al-zaman)," as said by Mujahid.

Abu Hurayra narrated that he said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to say, "Only the night and the day destroy us." But what destroys us is the one who causes us to die and gives us life. So this verse was revealed.

The third: "And nothing destroys us but death," as said by Qutrub. He recited a verse of Abu Dhu'ayb:

*Do you grieve over fate (al-manun) and its calamities? Time does not reproach the one who laments.*

The fourth: "And nothing destroys us but Allah," as said by Ikrimah.

al-Hasan narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Men say, 'Alas for the misfortune of time! Alas for the wretchedness of time!' Do not revile time, for indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Time (al-dahr). It is He who grasps the days and spreads them out."

His Exalted and Majestic saying: ﴿And you see every nation kneeling﴾. The ummah (nation) is the people of each religion (millah).

Regarding *al-jathiyah* (kneeling), there are five interpretations:

First: *mustawfizah*, meaning crouching on the toes, ready to rise. This was said by Mujahid.

Sufyan said: *al-mustawfiz* is the one of whom only his two knees and the tips of his fingers touch the ground.

Second: *mujtama'ah*, meaning gathered together. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

Third: *mutamayyizah*, meaning set apart. This was said by Ikrimah.

Fourth: *khadi'ah*, meaning humbled, in the dialect of Quraysh. This was said by Mu'arrij.

Fifth: *barikah 'ala al-rukab*, meaning sitting on the knees. This was said by al-Hasan.

Regarding *al-judhah* (kneeling), there are two views:

One: it refers to the disbelievers exclusively. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Second: it is general, covering both the believer and the disbeliever, while awaiting the reckoning.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah related from 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Babah that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is as if I see you on the mound, kneeling in front of Hell."

﴿Every nation is called to its record﴾. Concerning this there are three aspects:

First: to its reckoning. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

(p-268) Second: to its record, which was being copied for it, in which was recorded what it did of good and evil. This was said by al-Kalbi.

Third: to its book which was revealed to its messenger. This was related by al-Jahiz.

His Exalted and Majestic saying: ﴿This is Our record, speaking against you with truth﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions:

First: that it is the Qur'an, guiding you to what truth is in it, so it is as if it were a witness against you. This was said by Ibn Qutaybah.

Second: that it is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), which bears witness to what was decreed in it of happiness and misery, good and evil. This was said by Muqatil, and it is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid.

Third: that it is the book of deeds, in which the guardian angels (al-hafazah) write the deeds of the servants, and it bears witness against you by what it contains of the truthfulness of your deeds. This was said by al-Kalbi.

﴿Indeed We used to copy what you were doing﴾. Concerning this there are three aspects:

First: meaning the guardian angels write down what you were doing in the world. This was said by 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and by whoever holds that it is the book of deeds.

Second: that the guardian angels copy from the treasurers (al-khazanah) what is recorded with them of the states of the servants. This was said by Ibn Abbas, and by whoever holds that the Book is the Preserved Tablet.

Third: "We copy what the noble angels, the guardian angels, wrote down for you." This was said by al-Hasan, because the guardian angels raise the pages of deeds to the treasurers.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 45, verses 30–37:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And it will be said, "This Day We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day."﴾ On this there are three interpretations:

First: "This Day We will leave you in the Fire just as you left My command." This was said by al-Dahhak.

Second: "This Day We will leave you without mercy just as you left obedience," and this is a possibility.

Third: "This Day We will leave you without good just as you left Us without deeds." This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And to Him belongs the greatness (al-kibriya') in the heavens and the earth.﴾ On this there are four interpretations:

Third: that it is honour (al-sharaf). This was said by Ibn Ziyad.

﴿And He is the Mighty (al-'Aziz)﴾ in His retribution, ﴿the Wise (al-Hakim)﴾ in His governance.
